en.name: Gregory VII
en.summary: One of the most consequential reforming popes, whose Dictatus Papae asserted sweeping papal authority and whose conflict with Henry IV produced the famous penance at Canossa.
en.body: Gregory VII, formerly the monk Hildebrand who had shaped papal reform under several predecessors, pursued the Gregorian Reforms with uncompromising intensity, banning lay investiture of bishops and asserting in his Dictatus Papae that the pope alone could depose emperors. His resulting conflict with Henry IV escalated to mutual excommunication and deposition attempts; Henry's dramatic penitential wait barefoot in the snow outside Canossa in 1077 briefly resolved the crisis, but renewed conflict later drove Gregory into exile, where he died declaring, according to tradition, 'I have loved justice and hated iniquity, therefore I die in exile.'
